hints: Remove the modulus safely by comparing squares: $(x-4)^2<4(3x+1)^2$.
Factor the resulting difference of two squares, or solve the boundary equations $x-4=\pm2(3x+1)$.
Use the two critical values to test the three intervals and retain those where the strict inequality holds.
walkthrough:
Because both sides are strictly non-negative, square both sides to eliminate the absolute value signs:
$$(|x - 4|)^2 < (2|3x + 1|)^2$$
$$(x - 4)^2 < 4(3x + 1)^2$$

Rearrange all terms to one side to form a standard quadratic inequality:
$$0 < (36 - 1)x^2 + (24 + 8)x + (4 - 16)$$
$$35x^2 + 32x - 12 > 0$$

Find the critical values by solving the corresponding quadratic equation $35x^2 + 32x - 12 = 0$ by factorisation or the quadratic formula:
$$(7x - 2)(5x + 6) = 0$$
Setting each factor to zero gives:
$$7x - 2 = 0 \implies x = \dfrac{2}{7}$$
$$5x + 6 = 0 \implies x = -\dfrac{6}{5}$$

Alternatively, find the critical values by solving the two boundary linear equations:
$$x - 4 = 2(3x + 1) \implies x - 4 = 6x + 2 \implies -5x = 6 \implies x = -\dfrac{6}{5}$$
$$x - 4 = -2(3x + 1) \implies x - 4 = -6x - 2 \implies 7x = 2 \implies x = \dfrac{2}{7}$$

Determine the solution set for the inequality $35x^2 + 32x - 12 > 0$:
Since the leading coefficient $35 > 0$, the quadratic expression is positive strictly outside the roots:
$$x < -\dfrac{6}{5} \quad \text{or} \quad x > \dfrac{2}{7}$$
